guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why the market is giving USC substantial respect. Through four games, USC averaged 43.0 points and 500.3 yards while gaining 7.2 yards per play. Jayden Maiava completed 75.7% of his passes with 12 touchdowns and one interception over that stretch, so Washington faces an offense capable of creating separation quickly.

Where we differ is in how consistently USC can control this game on the ground. Washington ranks sixth in rush EPA defense, while USC's rushing offense ranks 89th. That does not neutralize Maiava, but it could make USC more dependent on its passing game and reduce the number of comfortable, low-variance drives available to the favorite.

We also see a path for Washington to sustain enough offense to remain competitive. Its rushing attack meets a USC run defense ranked 96th in rush EPA, and USC allowed 43 fourth-quarter points across its first four games. We are not treating that late-game split as proof of a recurring problem, but it reinforces our view that Washington has credible ways to stay within the margin.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the defining matchup is USC's rushing offense against Washington's rush defense. King Miller ran for 102 yards against Rutgers, and USC's running backs combined for 180 yards without a negative rushing attempt in that game. Washington presents a much different efficiency test. If we see Washington consistently force USC away from easy rushing success, the game becomes more dependent on Maiava producing through the air, which is the structure that best supports our position.

recent_game.fact: USC improved to 4-0 overall and 1-0 in Big Ten play with a 42-35 road win over Rutgers.
USC never trailed against Rutgers and produced 461 total yards at 7.3 yards per play.
USC averaged 5.9 yards per rush and 8.7 yards per pass attempt against Rutgers.
USC scored four offensive touchdowns, one defensive touchdown and two field goals against Rutgers.
USC converted 5 of 10 third downs against Rutgers, including 2 of 3 in the fourth quarter.
USC recorded six plays of at least 20 yards against Rutgers, evenly divided between runs and passes.
USC intercepted two Rutgers passes and accumulated 115 interception-return yards.

quarterback.fact: Quarterback Jayden Maiava completed 20 of 32 passes for 277 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions against Rutgers.
Maiava completed passes to nine different USC players against Rutgers.
Maiava completed 5 of 6 passes for 35 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter against Rutgers.
Through four games, Maiava had completed 87 of 115 passes for 1,173 yards, 12 touchdowns and one interception, with a 75.7% completion rate and 194.0 efficiency rating.
Maiava led the nation through four games in passing yards, passing touchdowns and points responsible for.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running back King Miller rushed 16 times for 102 yards and a touchdown against Rutgers, his second consecutive 100-yard game.
Miller led USC through four games with 338 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 64 carries.
Redshirt freshman running back Riley Wormley produced 54 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on four touches against Rutgers.
Freshman wide receiver Kayden Dixon-Wyatt led USC against Rutgers with five receptions for 77 yards and caught a two-point conversion.
Dixon-Wyatt led USC through four games with 18 receptions and 258 receiving yards, including two touchdown catches.
Sophomore wide receiver Corey Simms caught all four of his targets for a career-high 72 yards and his first collegiate touchdown against Rutgers.
Freshman tight end Mark Bowman caught three passes for 32 yards against Rutgers.
Five true freshmen started USC's season opener: wide receivers Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, Trent Mosley and Tron Baker, tight end Mark Bowman and defensive end Luke Wafle.
USC's offensive line allowed one sack and helped the offense average 5.9 yards per carry against Rutgers.
USC running backs combined for 180 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries against Rutgers without recording a negative rushing attempt.
Offensive lineman Tobias Raymond has started at every offensive-line position except right guard.

defensive_personnel.fact: Safety Prophet Brown returned an interception 99 yards for a touchdown against Rutgers.
Safety Christian Pierce recorded a game-high 11 tackles, an interception and two pass breakups against Rutgers.
Linebacker Deven Bryant recorded eight tackles against Rutgers and led USC through four games with 20 tackles.
Linebacker Desman Stephens II recorded seven tackles, a pass breakup and half a sack against Rutgers.
Defensive end Kameryn Crawford had six tackles and shared USC's only sack against Rutgers with Desman Stephens II.

injury_availability.fact: Safety Prophet Brown was back on the field in 2026 after missing the entire 2025 season because of a season-ending injury suffered during fall camp.
Kicker Caden Chittenden returned in 2026 after missing the entire 2025 season because of a season-ending fall-camp injury.
Wide receiver Tanook Hines returned from injury against Fresno State and subsequently caught three passes for 33 yards against Rutgers.
